rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Pesticides — insecticides, herbicides, fungicides — protect crops but carry ecological costs. Organochlorines like DDT persist for decades and biomagnify up food chains until fish-eating birds lay thin-shelled eggs; organophosphates and carbamates poison nerves by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase; pyrethroids offer lower mammalian toxicity.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Bioaccumulation vs biomagnification:** bioaccumulation is build-up within one organism; biomagnification is concentration rising up trophic levels.  ·  **Organochlorines vs organophosphates:** organochlorines are persistent axon poisons (DDT); organophosphates degrade faster but are acute acetylcholinesterase-inhibiting nerve poisons (malathion).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects clear sources, effects, and control measures for air, water, and soil pollution.  ·  Pesticides: types, effects, biomagnification, and resistance are a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***DDT and eggshell thinning*** — the classic biomagnification case in fish-eating birds.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Persistent, magnifying, resistant — the three sins of pesticides."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m): What is Integrated Pest Management?** — IPM combines tolerant varieties, crop rotation, biological control and pheromone traps, using pesticides only when pest numbers cross the economic threshold — minimising chemical use while keeping pests below damaging levels.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most likely items: biomagnification with DDT; why spraying worsens pests; organophosphate mechanism; IPM components.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The pesticide treadmill:** resistance and resurgence make spraying self-defeating — selection pressure is evolution in fast-forward.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Classes: organochlorines (DDT — persistent), organophosphates (malathion — acetylcholinesterase inhibitors), carbamates, pyrethroids, herbicides (2,4-D, glyphosate), fungicides.  ·  Effects: biomagnification (DDT → eggshell thinning in birds), non-target kills (bees, natural enemies), human poisoning, pest resurgence and resistance.  ·  Alternatives: IPM — tolerant varieties, rotation, biological control (ladybirds, Bt), pheromone traps, pesticides only at economic threshold.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Pyrethrins, the natural ancestors of pyrethroids, come from chrysanthemum flowers — one of the oldest botanical insecticides.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Chemical Arms Race in Agriculture Pesticides are chemicals used to kill pests — insects (insecticides), weeds (herbicides), fungi (fungicides), rodents (rodenticides). They protect crops and save lives from vector-borne disease, but their persistence, biomagnification and resistance make them a central environmental problem.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts | Term | Definition | |---|---| | **Pesticide** | Any chemical agent used to destroy pests | | **Persistence** | How long a pesticide remains active in the environment (DDT: decades) | | **Biomagnification** | Increase in pesticide concentration at successively higher trophic levels | | **Bioaccumulation** | Build-up of a pesticide within one…  ·  ## 3. Types of Pesticides | Class | Target | Examples | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **Organochlorines** | Insects | DDT, aldrin, dieldrin, endosulfan | Highly persistent, lipophilic, banned in many countries; DDT still permitted for malaria control in some settings | | **Organophosphates** | Insects | Malathion, parathion, chlorpyrifos | Break down faster but acutely toxic…
